# Adler & Rochefort — Private Client repositioning audit

**Phase 1 — audit only. Prepared 18 September 2026.**

Repository: `ownizo/adlerrochefort`, checkout `/home/hugo/adlerrochefort`. Audited commit: `f8e9bfe5e5d6bcb8e41c0fa2dac9381561b09e4e` (16 September 2026); GitHub origin HEAD matched that commit at audit time. Starting working tree was clean. This document is the only repository addition. No page, content source, form, metadata, schema, redirect, navigation or deployment was changed. No forms were submitted. Other Ownizo repositories and external application implementations were not inspected.

**Evidence and limits.** The audit enumerated all 439 HTML files under `public/`, parsed their titles, metadata, headings, links, forms and JSON-LD, reconciled sitemap entries, and searched repository text sources, scripts, data, functions, configuration and historical reports. Published HTML is the evidence for what this checkout serves; generators are evidence for maintenance behaviour, not proof that their current output matches published HTML. Previous audit files are historical evidence, not substitutes for inspecting code. Findings describe the repository snapshot, not a browser-verified production deployment. Visual observations concern markup/CSS hierarchy, not screenshot or accessibility testing. Rankings, conversions, insurer appointments, real claims experience, staffing and operational capacity cannot be established from website copy. Insurance/legal assertions below are **claims made by the site requiring confirmation**, not independent legal or coverage advice. The user's confirmation that the firm is a **non-tied insurance agent**, not a broker, is the controlling business premise.

All 24 requested sections follow. Appendices in this same document contain the complete physical-page inventory, detailed records for important pages, CTA destinations, and exhaustive term-match locations. Relative source links use GitHub line anchors; line numbers refer to the audited commit. Recommendations are provisional editorial dispositions, never instructions already executed. **KEEP** does not endorse shared legal copy. **MERGE** identifies an intent-consolidation candidate whose unique material must first be retained. No route retirement is prescribed without search/link evidence.

## 1. Executive Summary

**This is an existing specialist content estate with fragmented entry points, not a blank-slate Private Client project.** The repository has Portuguese, English and German Private Client landings; a substantial English Portugal specialist library; an English Spain commercial cluster and five Spain categories; German product, relocation and local pages; and nationality-specific American content. There are **no Spanish-language HTML pages and no `/es/` route** in this snapshot. Spain is a country market inside `/en/`, not a language version.

The most valuable assets are unusually concrete: reconstruction values, proportional settlement, agreed values, single-item and category limits, valuation evidence, security conditions, collections in transit, unoccupancy, household employers, yacht operation/lay-up, US liability expectations, fiduciary roles and portfolios across jurisdictions. Lagos and Tavira both have substantive English local guides. German has a dedicated Lagos page and distinct Quinta do Lago/Vilamoura material. These should survive repositioning.

The main obstacles are:

1. **Conflicting definitions of Private Clients.** Portuguese promises coordination of private assets; English Portugal leads with difficult-to-replace objects and specialist underwriting; German covers complex family risks; Spain expressly describes a review of ordinary product lines and cautiously qualifies specialist availability. No single household service specification unites them.
2. **Agency terminology conflicts at source level.** Self-identification as “broker”, “Versicherungsmakler” and “courtier” is widespread, including metadata, shared chrome and schema text. [scripts/lib/terminology-rules.mjs:8–20](../scripts/lib/terminology-rules.mjs#L8) explicitly acknowledges the agency registration but instructs the generators to retain broker vocabulary. Copy corrections alone would not be durable.
3. **Spain is structurally developed but operationally positioned as a newer/add-on market: answer B.** There are eight commercial pages, eighteen Spain articles and five categories, but no named specialist Spanish capacity, no requested Spanish micro-market pages and materially weaker promises. Existing limitations must be resolved through evidence, not hidden by stronger marketing.
4. **German is not simply a price-comparison site.** Its current body copy actively prioritises risk, claims and written explanation. Its acquisition identity remains German expats in Portugal, its free-quote remnants remain, and its specialist review form is much more intrusive than English. There is no meaningful Germany–Portugal–Spain service journey.
5. **Gatekeeper content exists, but a gatekeeper service does not.** Property-operation, travelling-staff and family-office liability articles are useful building blocks. There is no PA/EA delegation process, authority model or professional-representative intake.
6. **Claims exceed what the repository can prove.** Named underwriting routes in Portugal, interim cover, unlimited-value motor wording, cross-jurisdiction fiduciary cover, quantified price/claims examples and Spain passporting language need substantiation. Neither a guide nor a generator comment proves placeability.
7. **Architecture is maintained through overlapping processes.** Static published files, JSON article data, multiple landing generators and shared-chrome passes can diverge. The read-only freshness check reported zero failures but four warnings, including 318 files with chrome drift; it expressly excludes important Spain/template and editorial checks.

The priority is to define and substantiate one coordination service, preserve specialist knowledge, and align the four existing entry points. A large new page programme would compound duplication before fixing the proposition.

**Discovery and navigation.** English shared navigation distinguishes Spain products and links a Spain Private Client route, but labels Portugal “Collections & Valuables” in parts of the footer. Portuguese navigation exposes private-asset anchor sections and “Os Meus Seguros”. German navigation/footer is Portugal-product-led. Spain's separate menu is country-specific and its “Looking for Portugal?” switch goes to `/en/expat-insurance-portugal/`, not the corresponding Private Client page. Portuguese and English Private Client landings have no declared hreflang pair; neither does the German specialist page. Language selectors generally send these users to the other language's homepage; a contextual German body link to English Private Clients is not a reciprocal language mapping.

**Sitemaps and existing URL history.** `sitemap.xml` indexes `sitemap-pages.xml` (199 URLs) and `sitemap-blog.xml` (232): 431 total URLs. Existing redirects are evidence of prior decisions; none was changed.

## 4. Portugal Private Client Audit

**Portuguese landing.** `/private-clients/` already says “Proteção integrada do património privado” and “Coordenação, não venda avulsa” (`public/private-clients/index.html:232–240`). It covers high-value residences, art/collections/jewellery/wine, classic/high-value vehicles, marine, life and personal protection. Its four-stage process maps existing cover, consults markets, compares terms and supports issuance/claims (`:309–310`). Annual review, renewals and coordinated follow-up are explicitly promised in the FAQ (`:335`). These are valuable foundations for the family proposition.

Weaknesses: health/IPMI is not a prominent part of that household map; the page remains Portugal-focused; the insurer panel is not differentiated by product/country; “seguradoras e sindicatos” and Hiscox access need documentary support; it promises a 24-working-hour first response and alternatives within 48 hours (`:336`), which is not necessarily feasible for individually underwritten risk. Personal protection links directly into Os Meus Seguros (`:305`), while the footer makes proprietary AI policy management part of the firm identity (`:392`).

**English landing.** `/en/private-clients/` has the H1 “Cover for things that are difficult to replace”, a search title covering high-value homes/art/jewellery/marine, and six risk cards including possessions away from home. It distinguishes agreed value, single-item limits, proportional-rule waivers, geography, restoration and underwriting (`:193–200`); identifies Hiscox, Liberty Mutual through Innovarisk and specialty placement (`:206–221`); and asks for valuations, provenance, photographs, security and survey/claims history (`:234–242`). This is the most developed specialist entry point.

Its service identity is discreet and written: no names/photos published, email/WhatsApp, one person through renewal/claim (`:226–229`). That is stronger than prestige adjectives, but it is an operational promise needing consistency with actual data flows and staffing. “We handle the claim” (`:301`) should be distinguished from insurer decisions. The form is a proportionate first conversation: name/email, optional phone, asset categories, item location, valuation and existing cover. It does not ask for a representative role, several residences by country, renewal schedule, health needs or household ownership structures. A Spain contextual link exists, so cross-country linkage is not zero; it is not yet a common review process.

**Library.** English depth substantially exceeds Portuguese. The English collection, liability, staff, high-value home and marine materials live in several categories rather than under one family-navigation structure. Some late-added household articles finish with a generic free-home-comparison form. Product-level guides can remain useful SEO entry points while eventually handing off to a coordinated review; they need not all become luxury pages.

## 5. Spain Private Client Audit

Spain consists of the English expat hub plus home, health, landlord, car, life, mortgage-protection and Private Client commercial pages, eighteen Spain articles and five category pages. The Private Client category contains **two primary article cards**: `/en/blog/high-value-home-insurance-spain/` and `/en/blog/insurance-review-expats-spain/`. Other Spain articles cover family needs, second homes, non-resident owners, purchase, community cover, rentals, health/visa, cars and mortgage/life. This is more than one Spain page.

The specialist landing says “one coordinated review” but also “The underlying products are the same ones covered elsewhere on this site” (`public/en/private-clients-spain/index.html:417`). Its high-value-property section says the mechanics are the same as ordinary home insurance (`:259–260`); its art/jewellery FAQ promises only what can actually be placed (`:424–425`). That restraint is appropriate where capacity is unverified, but it does not establish parity with Portugal's all-risks/agreed-value offering. No Spanish specialist insurer is identified on the Private Client landing or its two category guides. Marbella and Costa del Sol occur only as examples in form placeholders, not as local service content.

The underlying source is unusually candid: `scripts/spain-cluster.data.mjs:10–26` records that no Spanish insurer appointment and no passport-notification completion were confirmed in the repository when written. Published footer/legal copy nevertheless says “operating in Spain on a cross-border basis”, and the Iberian nationality guide says “passported into Spain under Freedom of Services”. These are materially different evidential states. The old source comment may be stale; it is **not proof that authorization is absent today**. Phase 2 needs the actual current confirmation.

**Form.** `private-client-review-spain` collects name/email/required phone, country of residence, location in Spain, property ownership/count, vehicles, risks, preferred contact and notes. At `public/en/private-clients-spain/index.html:357`, the risk field is `<input type="checkboxes" ... name="interests">`, an invalid input type which falls back to a text input rather than the intended checkbox group. The generator's generic field renderer is the corresponding maintenance point. Six additional-product checkboxes appear despite source commentary saying Private Clients has no outbound cross-sell. Contact preference includes Phone while the body promises all communication in writing. Submission wording reverts to “prepare and discuss your quote”. No representative/authority or multi-country asset structure is provided.

**Chat is another country inconsistency.** `netlify/functions/lib/rag-snippets.mjs:1180–1193` tells Spain chat to say “one broker, several risks” and states categorically that property outside Spain is outside what the business can review or arrange. That would include Portugal if repeated literally, conflicting with the business’s own Portugal offer. The English Portugal system prompt (`netlify/functions/lib/system-prompts.mjs:59–61`, `:108–113`) calls the firm a broker registered as an agent. Its estimate instructions route ordinary home/health/car/life inputs to a pricing tool; no explicit specialist-home exclusion appears in those instructions. This is a **source-level risk**, not a tested live chat outcome. Preserve Spain safeguards against inventing insurer names, local offices and capacity while reviewing the cross-country hand-off.

**Spain is answer B: newer/add-on**, despite substantial structural investment. The problem is conditional capability, shallow specialist depth, weaker service times, no hyperlocal proof and an uneven return journey. Do not “fix” it by removing truthful capacity caveats before confirming the service.

## 6. Portugal vs Spain Comparison

| Dimension | Portugal | Spain | Material consequence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Positioning | PT asset coordination; EN specialist objects/underwriting | Household review across ordinary products | Same label, different buying expectation. |
| Tone | Confident, technical, discreet | Cautious, explanatory, availability-dependent | Country parity not yet demonstrated. |
| Products | Homes, valuables, art, wine, classic cars, marine, family liability; health elsewhere | Home/car/health/life/landlord/mortgage; valuables conditional | Specialist breadth is not mirrored. |
| Insurers | Hiscox; Liberty Mutual via Innovarisk; wider panel | No named specialist Spanish insurer | Logos/Portugal articles cannot substantiate Spanish placement. |
| Underwriting | Agreed values, worldwide scheduling, restoration, surveys | Rebuild/occupancy/security principles, ask what can be arranged | Missing Spanish wording/underwriting evidence. |
| Service times | EN written reply within 24h; PT 24 working hours/48h alternatives | “Within a few working days” | Different service promise; also distinguish acknowledgment from terms. |
| Service method | EN says no call required; one person through claim/renewal | Written English but form offers phone | Channel inconsistency. |
| Claims | EN “We handle the claim”; PT document/communicate | Review page links shared claims support | Role and achievable scope need one specification. |
| Forms | EN asset/valuation review; PT review categories | Property-count/vehicle/product coordination | Useful pieces exist, but no common family data model. |
| Required personal data | EN phone optional | Spain phone required; DE much more extensive | Friction differs by entry point. |
| Main CTA | Review / Pedir análise | Request a Private Client Review | Spain CTA is already close to future direction. |
| Navigation | General multilingual service/chrome variants | Dedicated Spain product navigation | Users move between different information systems. |
| Country link | EN PT page links Spain counterpart | Spain switch goes to Portugal expat hub | No reciprocal same-service doorway. |
| Article depth | Numerous distinct technical and local guides | Two core Private Client articles | Structural category presence overstates parity. |
| Local evidence | Lagos, Tavira, Golden Triangle, Comporta/Melides, Cascais etc. | None of requested Spanish locations appears in published substantive copy | No credible Spanish micro-market foundation yet. |
| SEO | EN Portugal title is asset/product-led | Spain title is Private Client-led | Distinct concepts, rather than country variants of one promise. |
| Schema | PT organization has Lisbon + Lagos addresses and Portugal scope; DE Lagos/PT | Spain Service uses Spain scope with Portuguese provider | Not inherently wrong; organization identity and service geography need separation/consistency. |
| Hreflang | No PT/EN/DE Private Client pairing | English only, no `/es/` | Country selector must not masquerade as language selector. |
| Footer | PT AI/platform language; EN wider dual-country/footer links | Separate concise English footer with country products | Brand/service identity changes between journeys. |
| Regulation | Agency registration alongside broker self-description | ASF identity plus cross-border operating assertions | Terminology and passporting evidence both need review. |
| Visual hierarchy (source) | PT early form/asset sections; EN technical matrix and long guide index | Expat-style country menu, product sections, review form, short guides | Different content emphasis; no rendered visual parity asserted. |

## 7. `/de/` Audit

**23 pages, with a real specialist foundation.** Four standard consumer product pillars (health/home/car/life), one Private Client page, nine regional/local pages, relocation/health-continuity/vehicle-import/property-status material and two professional-liability pages surround the homepage. This is predominantly a **Germany-to-Portugal resident/owner proposition**, not a HNW Iberian household proposition. It is nevertheless inaccurate to call the current copy uniformly cheap-insurance-led.

**What is already good.** The homepage says “Wir beginnen nicht mit dem Preis. Wir beginnen mit Ihrem Risiko.” (`public/de/index.html:231`) and discusses policy differences, actual liability expectations, earthquake cover and claims assistance without guaranteeing settlement (`:327–330`). It adapts German assumptions: GKV/PKV, Anwartschaft, S1, Schadenfreiheitsklasse, household liability and underinsurance. It explicitly explains that service is in written English, despite German acquisition content (`:222–224`). These are substantive adaptations, not a literal generic English translation. Germany dominates; Austrian/Swiss specifics are not developed.

**Audience and hierarchy.** Its SEO title remains “Versicherungsmakler für deutsche Expats in Portugal”; standard health/home/car/life comes before Private Clients in the main product sequence. Private Clients is one risk category rather than the organising service. Local pages still target “deutsche Expats und Eigentümer”. Entrepreneurs/therapists broaden the audience further. That does not make these pages worthless; they should not set the eventual affluent-family hub's primary identity.

**Every price-language location is indexed in Appendix E.** Important live examples: homepage “Ihr kostenloses Angebot” (`:426`), “kostenlos und unverbindlich” comparison (`:400`), “Markt vergleichen” and insurer-portfolio comparison (`:243`, `:336–337`); house page “Versicherung vergleichen”; professional-indemnity page offers free competitor-proposal review. Conversely, mentions of “günstig” in vehicle tax or a warning against cheap earthquake exclusions are not a promise of cheap insurance. “not the lowest price” is evidence supporting the future positioning, not a commodity violation. No conclusion about discount positioning is based merely on counting the word Preis.

**Technology.** All 23 German pages contain the footer link “Zu MyCoverVault”. No visible “Adler One” wording was found in `/de/`; do not invent that problem. The homepage does not lead its core service narrative with SaaS. Footer product escape paths remain a secondary distraction.

**Terminology.** Makler/Versicherungsmakler occurs across titles, metadata, hero trust statements, body, FAQs, legal text and source modules. The source explicitly enforces it. “Makler” in the house-value discussion can mean an estate agent rather than Adler & Rochefort; the occurrence registry retains such cases for contextual review instead of indiscriminate replacement. Schema `InsuranceAgency` is not itself the offending term; descriptive fields/FAQ answers can contain it.

**Specialist page.** `/de/private-clients-portugal/` covers homes, multiple residences, art/collections, agreed-value jewellery, classic cars, IPMI, liability and marine. Hiscox/Liberty Mutual/Innovarisk are named. It has useful underwriting-process explanation and an English specialist link. However, broad “Ja” availability statements and worldwide cover require real underwriting evidence. It has **no Spain link**, and no German Spain page exists.

**Critical form mismatch.** The current `de-private-clients-wizard` (`public/de/private-clients-portugal/index.html:354–405`) requires NIF, date of birth, full address, postcode, phone, email, nationality, tax residency, start date and consent. It has **no visible assets, existing insurance, valuations, representative role or message field**. The hidden `dados_dinamicos` input is not evidence of a visible needs assessment. The homepage's different conditional form actually collects `pc_werte`, property count, total approximate value and requirements. Source `scripts/de-content/private-clients.mjs` still describes an asset-context message-based form, so the source/rendered divergence is material. A prospect without a Portuguese NIF faces an inappropriate barrier to an initial review.

**Local depth.** Lagos is already its own German route. Quinta do Lago and Vilamoura have distinct technical treatments; Comporta is strong on construction/fire response. Tavira was deliberately omitted by an earlier source decision (`scripts/de-content/local.mjs:3–13`), despite the substantive existing English Tavira guide. That prior rationale is incompatible with treating Tavira as a required future micro-market, but no page was added. Cascais references Costa do Estoril; there is no dedicated Estoril page. Mallorca/Costa del Sol are absent.

**Conclusion.** Reposition its hierarchy and review journey while preserving German-specific explanatory work. Do not label all German content mass-market or erase Lagos/central/eastern differences.

## 8. British Content Map

**Explicit British content:** `/en/blog/british-expats-brexit-insurance-portugal/` and the British section of `/en/blog/insurance-portugal-spain-international-residents/`. Existing relocation/visa, resident health and S1/GHIC-related discussions support post-Brexit questions. There is no dedicated British Private Client hub; English language alone is not proof of British targeting.

**Portugal assets/lifestyle:** `/en/second-home-insurance-portugal/`, `/en/unoccupied-home-insurance-portugal/`, holiday-home and unoccupancy guides, high-value-home/valuables/vehicle/marine guides, domestic staff and two-jurisdiction portfolio articles all address plausible British owner needs. The local guides for Lagos, Quinta do Lago/Vale do Lobo/Vilamoura, Sintra/Cascais and broader coastal/golf property are particularly reusable. Praia da Luz has one worked liability scenario, not a location hub. Estoril is contextual, not a standalone British landing.

**Spain:** English second-home, non-resident-property, family, purchase, health and car/import guides are relevant to British buyers. Their British relevance is generally inferred from circumstances rather than bespoke HNW adaptation. No Marbella, Benahavís, Nueva Andalucía, Sotogrande or Mallorca page exists. The Iberian guide supplies an initial cross-border bridge, but there is no complete UK–Portugal–Spain family asset/review flow or art-transport itinerary linking those places.

Priority distinction for later work: preserve residency/health education as supporting material while elevating occupancy, rebuilding, moving valuables, local claims coordination and household employment in the Private Client path. No British pages were created.

## 9. American Content Map

The American estate is unusually developed and should not be treated as missing. It includes `/en/insurance-for-americans-in-portugal/` and guides on insurance when moving, health for Americans, Portugal/USA health, US driving records, US-perspective claims, umbrella versus Portuguese liability and American property buyers. Appendix A lists exact routes, and Appendix B captures their headings and metadata.

**Specific strengths:** `/en/blog/us-buyers-property-cover-portugal/` distinguishes construction cost from transaction price, company ownership, non-residency, incoming possessions and payment-diversion risk. `/en/blog/us-umbrella-vs-portuguese-liability-insurance/` explains that familiar US excess structures should not be assumed to carry across, and explicitly defers interpretation of US policies to the US carrier/adviser. The rebuilding, sum-insured, agreed-value, worldwide-possessions and international-health guides complete a useful education path. Some sweeping US/Portuguese comparisons still need wording-level verification.

**Geography:** American property copy explicitly mentions Lisbon, Cascais, Algarve and Comporta. General local content adds Estoril context and Melides through the combined Comporta/Melides guide. These are not all American-specific local pages. No American Spain hub or requested Spanish micro-market exists. The Spain content can attract Americans but does not explain US-to-Spain coverage expectations at comparable depth.

**Gaps:** high-value rented residences as a distinct American scenario; a coordinated Portugal-and-Spain family inventory; actual available liability/excess limits; US jurisdiction restrictions; valuables moving between multiple residences and health coverage including/excluding the US under one documented review. The topic “multiple residences” exists; the operational Iberian family service is what remains incomplete.

## 12. Gatekeeper Audit

### Personal Assistant / Executive Assistant

A “personal assistant” appears in the travelling-private-staff article as someone travelling with the household, **not as a purchaser/delegated insurance administrator** (`public/en/blog/insurance-private-staff-travel-household/index.html:412`). Valuation/documentation guides, records of serial numbers, security requirements, renewals and written claims explanations can support an eventual PA checklist. No substantive Executive Assistant proposition, authority-to-instruct process, principal/representative distinction, delegated document access or renewal-administration workflow was found. “Delegated authority” in MGA articles is insurer underwriting authority and must not be counted as PA delegation.

### Property Manager / House Manager / Estate Manager

Relevant material already covers unoccupancy, keyholders/inspections, water damage, alarms, pools/private access, staff quarters, contractors, renovations, rental use, inventory and claims. `/en/blog/non-resident-property-insurance-spain/` explicitly mentions a local property manager/keyholder (`:210`); `/en/blog/us-buyers-property-cover-portugal/` describes a manager/keyholder as a possible condition (`:240`); the landlord page asks who manages locally. The condominium form includes “Property manager”. These are credible supporting signals, not a dedicated professional-facing service. There is no general house/estate-manager hub, multi-principal authority process, maintenance evidence handover, or professional referral service specification for private homes. Commercial real-estate referral/commission pages are adjacent but not equivalent.

### Family Office

`/en/blog/fiduciary-family-office-liability-portugal/` is substantial: trusts/foundations, fiduciary versus ordinary D&O, jurisdiction, Side A/run-off and advisers. It explicitly mentions private bankers and trust-company officers and says Adler & Rochefort can arrange cover across the relevant jurisdictions (`:476`), which requires particularly careful capacity verification. The travelling-staff article distinguishes family-office/company employment from domestic employment. Portuguese American-investment content mentions family offices in an investment narrative. None establishes an ongoing local household coordination layer, consolidated reporting, instruction authority or renewal/claims interface for a family office. Preserve the distinction between **insuring fiduciary liability** and **servicing a family's insurance on a family office's instructions**.

## 13. Legal / Terminology Consistency

The user's confirmed status is Ownizo, Unipessoal Lda., trading as Adler & Rochefort, a non-tied insurance agent registered with ASF. Broad market access must not be equated with being a broker, nor agency status with one-insurer dependence.

**Root conflict:** `scripts/lib/terminology-rules.mjs:8–20` says the entity is an *agente de seguros*, but retains broker/courtier/Versicherungsmakler based on peer marketing usage. `EN_BROKER` includes explicit “intermediary → broker” mappings. `scripts/phase2-terminology.mjs`, `scripts/terminology.mjs` and `scripts/block0-compliance.mjs` consume these rules. Existing historical audit reports can therefore call broker wording “corrected” under a premise this brief rejects. Do not use those reports as legal authority.

**Published examples:** English Private Clients meta description and body `:221`, Spain meta description “one broker” and body `:255`, German homepage title/hero/FAQ/legal text, French `courtier`, shared “Why Use a Broker” navigation, the dedicated `/en/why-use-an-insurance-broker/` route, English legal notices and Organization/FAQ descriptions. Portuguese mostly uses mediador/agente, which should not be falsely flagged as broker synonyms requiring removal.

**Complete location register:** Appendix D includes all matching source locations, not just important pages: visible text, attributes/metadata, JSON-LD, URL/anchor names, generator strings, article data, functions and historical reports. It also includes generic/third-party occurrences so no automatic replacement is implied. Names in external third-party links, estate-agent “Makler”, quotations and legal definitions require context. A standard schema type `InsuranceAgency` is consistent with an agency and is not a defect merely because visible copy is wrong.

**Market access distinctions.** “Not tied to one insurer” is useful and consistent with the brief. Named preferred carriers or a “selected panel” chosen for conditions/claims are not evidence of restricted legal access. German “innerhalb unseres Versichererportfolios” and source comments limiting comparison to seven panel names can, however, make the consumer infer a narrow fixed universe. That inference is different from a factual claim of exclusive appointment. No conclusion that the firm is actually tied to one insurer is supported by this audit. The narrative should eventually distinguish broad access, actual appointments, MGA access and quality-led selection without promising the entire market or every product. The source seven-name panel is not a verified country/product capacity matrix.

**Other material inconsistencies:** Portugal and Germany vary between “registered” and stronger authorization/service language; Spain source comments and published passporting claims diverge; PT Private Client organization schema lists Lisbon and Lagos while DE/Spain provider records use Lagos. Confirm the real office/service locations before treating either representation as wrong. English articles sometimes retain Portuguese “mediador registado…” disclaimers. These are consistency findings, not an assertion of unlawful activity.

## 15. Price-Led / Commodity Language

Appendix E records matched price/free/comparison wording with source locations and page context. The strongest conflicts are CTA modules attached to technical articles: the art-collection, two-jurisdiction portfolio, domestic-staff, unoccupancy, pools and local-property guides repeatedly close with free home comparison. The international-children-health and frequent-traveller evacuation articles lead back to free health quotes. German's homepage still says “Ihr kostenloses Angebot”. Standard health/car cost articles and bank-switching guides are relevant acquisition content but should not define the specialist service.

**Do not equate every price reference with commodity selling.** The English Private Client statement that a suitable retail policy may do the same job for less is useful impartial advice; German rejects price-first recommendations; explanations of how additional premium buys meaningful liability or removes exclusions can be substantive. Indicative local premium tables nevertheless require evidence and dating, and their presence changes the user's expectation from risk assessment towards shopping.

No claim that the whole site promises the lowest price is justified. The problem is mixed intent and hand-off. Existing price-led product routes can be preserved outside the core household coordination journey.

## 16. Technology References

Appendix F indexes every matched named-product/portal/AI-management reference across website and source files; source-only identifiers, URLs, historical records and current visible copy are distinguished. These are references found **inside this repository**; the external products themselves were not audited.

- **Os Meus Seguros:** PT homepage anchors `#adler-one` and `#adler-pro`, desktop/mobile navigation, Private Client personal-protection section, footer/platform access and PT/EN SaaS articles. PT Private Clients explicitly promotes tracking all managed policies on the platform. This materially competes with specialist coordination as the reason to choose the firm.
- **MyCoverVault:** English and localized footer links, including every German page and English Portugal Private Clients. A returning-client utility link can support administration; it is neutral if subordinate, distracting if presented as the service's strategic differentiator. Spain uses a separate footer without this same emphasis.
- **Adler One / Adler Pro:** exact names and legacy anchor/route/source references are retained in the appendix. A slug such as `adler-pro-saas-platform` may now display Os Meus Seguros; do not misreport the slug as current visible branding. No visible Adler One label was found in German pages.
- **AI / digital policy management:** shared proprietary-AI/PT footer language, platform articles and homepage sections are stronger SaaS signals than the English specialist body. Chat widget references are a distinct support channel, not proof of a client policy portal or an AI-managed Private Client service.

Netlify contains vault-related header settings, but there is **no physical `/vault/` HTML route in the 439-file corpus**. Configuration references do not prove a live portal implementation. The policy-intake notification/classification functions are part of this public-site repository and were inspected as journey evidence; no external CRM/application was accessed.

## 18. SEO Cannibalisation Risks

**High-risk overlaps:** Private Client Portugal landing versus luxury-home and valuables overviews; art-collection and art/valuables guides; three staff articles; home general/multirisk/protect/second/holiday/unoccupied routes; overlapping evacuation and health comparison/pre-existing-condition pages. The new coordination proposition should not compete for every product keyword itself.

**Potentially legitimate separation:** luxury/high-value-home transactional research versus second-home occupancy; rebuilding-value method versus bank sum insured versus waiver-of-average; single-item jewellery scheduling versus travelling worldwide; boat purchase/import versus navigation/private-charter versus winter lay-up; local Lagos versus Tavira. These answer different questions and should not be merged just because they share vocabulary.

**Spain:** high-value-home guide and Private Client landing are useful informational/commercial counterparts. The review article and `/en/insurance-review/` need a clear distinction between editorial explanation and form utility. Generic national content should not be multiplied into eight location variants without local evidence.

Titles, H1s and descriptions often deliberately differ: English PC title lists assets while its H1 is “Cover for things that are difficult to replace”; German uses expat/Makler SEO wording but risk-led body copy. That is not an automatic SEO error, but it communicates different propositions at different entry points. Actual cannibalisation/ranking loss is **not established** without current Search Console query/page data. The repository's historical `audit/cannibalization.*` and query-ownership files help trace intent but do not prove current performance.

## 20. Content That Conflicts With the New Positioning

**Commodity-driven conflicts:** free comparison modules on specialist property/staff/collection pages; general health/motor price acquisition mixed into Private Client journeys; German free-offer close and identity-first wizard; Spain form reverting to quote language. These are documented page-level conflicts, not a recommendation to remove the ordinary consumer business.

**Superficial prestige:** the Portuguese American-investment article foregrounds capital, luxury, premium and prestige, whereas its redirected English successor focuses on specific insurance differences. The word “luxury” in the English high-value-home/car slugs is not alone a reason to retire them: their current H1s and bodies are mostly technical. “Premium” often means an insurance premium, and “exclusive” can occur in exclusions/security descriptions; Appendix G treats these as matches, not automatic negative classifications.

**Service mismatch:** English Portugal promises individually underwritten cover; Spain denies being a luxury product and describes ordinary underlying products; PT includes platform-led protection; Germany combines complex-risk language with transactional personal-data intake. A family buying coordinated service cannot infer the same experience from these pages.

**Wrong identity:** all firm self-references as broker/corretor/Makler/courtier equivalents conflict with the brief. Source-level correction will eventually be necessary, but none was performed.

**Too strong or unsupported:** “no ceiling” motor value, general worldwide claims, interim cover, cross-jurisdiction fiduciary placement, hard underwriting/claims universals and unsupported numerical local claims. These require proof rather than mere stylistic improvement.

## 21. Product / Capacity Claims That Require Verification

**The repository establishes that a claim is published, not that capacity exists.** No audited appointment schedule, current insurer wording set, binding authority evidence, or product-by-country placement matrix was found in the inspected content/configuration corpus. The following register separates editorial capability from verified operations.

| Medium | PT 24h/48h alternatives, EN 24h, German 24 Arbeitsstunden, Spain days | Agreed acknowledgment/advice/quote service standards and working-day definitions. |
| Medium | Local premium tables, €150k–€400k schedule omissions, example claim amounts, “most common” loss statements | Anonymised experience or illustrative labels, dated assumptions, source support and insurer variability. |
| Medium | Market-wide absolutes: all policies, always, never, regulatory construction/territory statements | Qualified technical/legal review against actual wordings; avoid treating examples as universal rules. |

Named insurer logos/panel chips are **marketing evidence only**. Distinguish confirmed operational placement, proposed access and educational discussion in Phase 2. The generic Spain disclaimer is not a substitute for verifying the more definite claims elsewhere.

## 22. Architecture Constraints

1. **Published files and sources both matter.** `public/` is deployed as-is. Blog data lives in `data/articles.json`; separate content/build files generate country, language, location and commercial pages. Several scripts execute writes at import time. They were not run for generation in this audit.
2. **Shared chrome has multiple owners.** `scripts/lib/partials.mjs`, `chrome.mjs`, `blog-parts.mjs`, `spain-chrome.mjs`, language-cluster modules and hand-authored pages do not share one universal header/footer. Applying a general pass can overwrite bespoke intent.
3. **Read-only freshness result:** zero failures, four warnings: chrome stale across 318 distinct files (topBar 214, footer 318, cookie 312, nav 220, landingNav 2, landingDrawer 2); `public/css/ar-site.css` differs from its builder; both PT/EN feeds each contain one unexpected latest-30 article. The first sandboxed attempt could not complete a subprocess; an authorized read-only rerun completed. This is a maintenance finding, not a reason to regenerate during Phase 1. The checker explicitly excludes Spain chrome and editorial correctness and does not prove all sources are in sync.
4. **Language and country are different dimensions.** Spain is `/en/*-spain/`; Portuguese has root URLs; German has `/de/`; nationality hubs use a third pattern. Region is usually an article slug, not a typed content dimension. One mirrored URL naming convention does not presently exist.
5. **No core PC language pair.** `scripts/lib/lang-pairs.mjs` and separate hreflang/market maps do not establish a PT/EN/DE Private Client equivalence. They must not be paired blindly: current content is not equivalent. Spain is not a Spanish translation.
6. **Root routing is language-based.** `netlify/edge-functions/lang-router.ts` redirects only `/`, uses a PT/EN preference cookie, and otherwise maps browser languages to localized homepages. Spanish browsers fall through to English. It is not a country or Private Client router.
7. **Form data models diverge.** PT `private-clients-review`, EN `valuables-review`, ES `private-client-review-spain`, DE `de-private-clients-wizard`, and generic `international-insurance-review` have different fields and classification. `netlify/functions/lib/lead-classification.mjs` maps them; dynamic fields, validators, wizard scripts, notification handling and analytics would all need consideration later. No external CRM was audited.
8. **One-country intake.** The international review utility chooses Portugal or Spain and shows country-specific products. Portugal's options omit Private Client Review, while Spain includes it. This is not a unified two-country household intake.
9. **Generator drift is concrete.** German specialist source expects context fields while published HTML uses a personal-data wizard; Spain's field renderer emits an invalid `checkboxes` input. The dedicated source/generator needs reconciliation before any later regeneration.
10. **Terms are actively normalized to the wrong brief.** Existing terminology enforcement would restore broker vocabulary. Metadata, schema descriptions, shared text, notifications/chat material and archived reports must be distinguished before any future replacement process.
11. **Indexing and redirects are separate assets.** Sitemaps use actual files and article status; drafts/merged entries differ from live files; permanent history lives in `public/_redirects`. Existing merged slugs must not be recreated accidentally. Missing `/es/` is a true absence, not evidence to invent it as a requirement.
12. **Visual parity is not guaranteed by common colours.** Separate CSS families and inline styles support different menu/form/card hierarchies. A later design phase needs rendered desktop/mobile review after content/service decisions; this audit did not assert visual or functional production equivalence.

## 23. Unknowns / Questions Before Phase 2

Only material decisions not answerable from this repository:

1. What exact Spain passporting/operating permissions and insurer/MGA appointments are current, and what documentary evidence can support public statements?
2. Which product/territory/value combinations can actually be placed today, especially art/transit, collections, high-value vehicles, yachts, excess liability, fiduciary roles and travelling staff? Which are referrals rather than direct arrangements?
3. What is the real coordinated service: review scope, renewals, valuations, claims assistance, responsible adviser/deputy, response times and fee/remuneration basis?
4. Can one family receive coordinated service for both countries through one file/contact, while policies remain country-appropriate? Which cross-border activities are expressly outside scope?
5. What authorization and information-sharing process supports a PA, property manager or family office acting for a principal? Who may instruct changes and receive sensitive asset information?
6. Is German acquisition with written English servicing the deliberate long-term model? Are Austrian/Swiss circumstances within scope or only Germany-derived explanations?
7. Which location experience and actual case evidence can substantiate requested Spanish micro-markets and Germany-focused Tavira/Praia da Luz material? Are existing worked cases factual, anonymised or illustrative?
8. What current query/page performance and backlinks should govern consolidation choices? No destructive URL decision should rely solely on textual overlap.
9. Which offices, service geographies, privacy assurances and market-access descriptions are factually approved for public use, including the Lisbon/Lagos schema difference?

## 24. Recommended Phase 2 Scope

A bounded next phase should: establish the verified service/capacity matrix; define one household coordination proposition and its country limits; decide the roles of the four existing Private Client landings; agree accurate multilingual agency/market-access terminology; reconcile review forms and representative authority needs; preserve and rationalise the technical library; resolve high-confidence overlap after performance review; specify a German audience/locality plan that keeps **Lagos, Golden Triangle and Tavira separate**; and research Spanish locality/capacity gaps before authorising location pages. Then specify coherent navigation, language/country relationships, metadata/schema and source ownership, with explicit migration and validation requirements.

This is a proposed implementation **scope**, not a redesign. No future hub, audience page, nationality page, location page, CTA, redirect or production change has been implemented.

- [public/blog/investimento-americano-luxo-portugal/index.html:840](../public/blog/investimento-americano-luxo-portugal/index.html#L840): “Mas investir num mercado novo, à distância e num quadro regulatório diferente, traz uma camada de risco que muitos investidores subestimam. Avaliações de capital desatualizadas, apólices traduzidas à pressa, coberturas que não dialogam entre o imobiliário, o turismo e a holding — são lacunas que só aparecem quando há um sinistro. A Adler & Rochefort posiciona-se precisamente aqui: como o parceiro local que dá ao inve…”

- [public/blog/investimento-americano-luxo-portugal/index.html:854](../public/blog/investimento-americano-luxo-portugal/index.html#L854): “Uma vila de luxo, um apartamento de topo em Lisboa ou uma propriedade na Comporta não são imóveis comuns. Têm valores de reconstrução elevados, acabamentos e materiais difíceis de repor, sistemas domóticos, arte, adegas e, muitas vezes, períodos longos sem ocupação porque o proprietário reside nos Estados Unidos.”

- [public/blog/investimento-americano-luxo-portugal/index.html:898](../public/blog/investimento-americano-luxo-portugal/index.html#L898): “O maior risco para um investidor americano não é o sinistro em si — é descobrir, tarde demais, que a cobertura não correspondia ao que pensava ter contratado. Diferenças entre a prática seguradora dos Estados Unidos e a portuguesa, traduções imprecisas, capitais mal dimensionados e a falta de um interlocutor de confiança no terreno são as causas mais frequentes de surpresas desagradáveis.”

- [public/blog/subseguro-portugal/index.html:842](../public/blog/subseguro-portugal/index.html#L842): “O Regime Jurídico do Contrato de Seguro (Decreto-Lei n.º 72/2008, artigo 76.º) estabelece a chamada regra proporcional: se o capital seguro for inferior ao valor do interesse seguro no momento do sinistro, a seguradora só paga a indemnização na proporção entre o capital contratado e o valor real do bem — mesmo que o sinistro seja apenas parcial.”

- [public/blog/subseguro-portugal/index.html:844](../public/blog/subseguro-portugal/index.html#L844): “Um exemplo torna isto concreto. Uma moradia está segurada por 250.000 €, mas o custo de reconstrução atual é de 400.000 €. Um incêndio na cozinha causa 40.000 € de danos. Em vez de receber os 40.000 € do prejuízo, o proprietário recebe 40.000 × (250.000 ÷ 400.000) = 25.000 €. A diferença de 15.000 € fica a cargo do segurado — por um sinistro que nem sequer destruiu o imóvel todo.”

Genau das ist der konkrete Beweis für unsere Positionierung: Wir beginnen nicht mit dem Preis, sondern mit dem Risiko.”

- [public/de/krankenversicherung-portugal/index.html:310](../public/de/krankenversicherung-portugal/index.html#L310): “Der wesentliche Unterschied liegt in der Aufnahme: Eine mutualistische Mitgliedschaft funktioniert über die Mitgliedschaft selbst statt über individuelle Risikoprüfung, wodurch das Höchstaufnahmealter der klassischen Versicherer dort nicht in gleicher Form gilt. Für jemanden Anfang siebzig, der gerade in Portugal ankommt, ist das oft der einzige realistische Weg zu privater Deckung.”

- [public/de/krankenversicherung-portugal/index.html:348](../public/de/krankenversicherung-portugal/index.html#L348): “Ja. Die meisten regulären Versicherer haben ein Höchstaufnahmealter für neue Policen. Darüber führt in der Regel nur die mutualistische Route (z. B. MGEN) zu privater Deckung, da sie auf Mitgliedschaft statt individueller Risikoprüfung basiert.”

- [public/en/blog/coastal-clifftop-properties-algarve-subsidence-erosion-flood/index.html:216](../public/en/blog/coastal-clifftop-properties-algarve-subsidence-erosion-flood/index.html#L216): “Portuguese wordings, like wordings everywhere, insure sudden and accidental events. Coastal erosion is neither: it is a gradual, certain, ongoing process, and no insurer in any market will fund it. That is not a gap in your policy, it is the boundary of what insurance is. What is insurable is the sudden event — a storm, a collapse, an inundation — and the question at underwriting is how likely the location makes one.”

- [public/en/blog/coastal-clifftop-properties-algarve-subsidence-erosion-flood/index.html:225](../public/en/blog/coastal-clifftop-properties-algarve-subsidence-erosion-flood/index.html#L225): “A coastal villa that presents well is not dramatically more expensive to insure than an inland one. Two conditions, both binding, both easy to miss.”

If the sum insured is lower than the true value of the insured property, the insurer settles claims in the same proportion. Insure a €1,000,000 rebuild for €600,000 and you are 60 per cent insured; a €100,000 water-damage claim is settled at €60,000, less the excess. - [public/en/blog/outdated-insured-values/index.html:209](../public/en/blog/outdated-insured-values/index.html#L209): “Rebuild cost is labour, materials and professional fees at today's prices. It has moved substantially over the last five years, and a figure set before that period understates the rebuild even if nothing about the house has changed.”

- [public/en/blog/outdated-insured-values/index.html:245](../public/en/blog/outdated-insured-values/index.html#L245): “The rule does not work in reverse. Insuring a €600,000 rebuild for €1,000,000 does not produce a larger settlement — indemnity is capped at the loss actually suffered — it simply produces a larger premium every year. Over-declaration is common on properties insured at purchase price rather than rebuild cost, and on modern cars still insured at what they cost new. It is quieter than underinsurance and it is not free.”

In August a guest’s child pulled a wall-mounted television off its bracket, damaging the screen and the plaster, and in the same stay a barbecue scorched the terrace. - [public/en/blog/second-home-rent-out-holiday-let-standard-home-cover/index.html:234](../public/en/blog/second-home-rent-out-holiday-let-standard-home-cover/index.html#L234): “The reason it is worth recounting is what happened next. The owner made the claim, and the claim itself disclosed the letting. The insurer did not pay, cancelled the policy at renewal, and the property then had to be placed with a disclosure of a cancelled policy on the record — which narrowed the market and raised the premium for three years. A €2,100 problem became a five-figure one over the life of the property.”

- [public/en/blog/second-home-rent-out-holiday-let-standard-home-cover/index.html:245](../public/en/blog/second-home-rent-out-holiday-let-standard-home-cover/index.html#L245): “The uplift is smaller than most owners assume. On a typical Algarve townhouse, the difference between a second-home policy and a properly written holiday-let policy is usually €150 to €350 a year. On a villa with a pool it might be €250 to €450. Against eleven weeks of summer income, that is a fraction of a single booking.”

- [public/en/private-clients/index.html:161](../public/en/private-clients/index.html#L161): “Some property does not fit a Portuguese off-the-shelf policy. A contents section caps any single item at a few thousand euros. A buildings sum insured set from a purchase price triggers the proportional rule. A motor policy settles on a depreciated market value. None of that is a defect in the product — it is what the product was built for.”

- [public/en/private-clients/index.html:162](../public/en/private-clients/index.html#L162): “The alternative is individually underwritten cover: an underwriter looks at the specific risk, agrees a value in advance, schedules the items that need scheduling, and writes the conditions into the contract before anything happens. It takes days rather than minutes, and it requires paperwork from you. This page sets out how it works and what it needs.”

- [public/en/private-clients/index.html:173](../public/en/private-clients/index.html#L173): “policy insures contents to a total sum, then caps what it will pay for any one item within that total. The cap is typically a few thousand euros, or a stated percentage of the contents sum with a per-item ceiling on top. A watch worth €60,000 inside a €150,000 contents figure is not insured for €60,000; it is insured for whatever the single-article limit says, and the rest of the contents sum is irrelevant to it.”

## Appendix D — Broker-equivalent terminology: every repository match


Includes English broker/brokerage; Portuguese corretor/corretora; German Makler/Versicherungsmakler; French courtier; Dutch makelaar; Danish mægler; Swedish mäklar variants; Chinese 经纪人/保险经纪; and Hebrew intermediary candidates. Generic profession, estate-agent, third-party, URL/code and historical occurrences are retained for review. Hebrew agency wording is not automatically a broker error. Correct Portuguese mediador/agente and schema InsuranceAgency are not treated as broker mistakes. The firm-specific contradictions and source rules are assessed in §13.


**Coverage:** 2784 raw matches across 380 files. Every match has a 1-based line and character column below; the file link opens its complete source. These counts include deliberate duplicates (metadata, JSON-LD, rendered pages, generators, archived reports), not 2784 unique editorial errors. A matched term is a review flag, not an automatic finding that the wording refers to Adler & Rochefort.

## Appendix E — Price/free/comparison language: occurrence register


This is a literal-match review index, including source strings and historical reports. A free review is not identical to cheapest-price selling. Negated price claims, warning examples, ordinary insurance premiums and competing offers must be read in context; §7 and §15 distinguish these. The scope includes the full repository so shared modules cannot hide private-client exposure.


**Coverage:** 1619 raw matches across 344 files. Every match has a 1-based line and character column below; the file link opens its complete source. These counts include deliberate duplicates (metadata, JSON-LD, rendered pages, generators, archived reports), not 1619 unique editorial errors. A matched term is a review flag, not an automatic finding that the wording refers to Adler & Rochefort.

## Appendix F — Technology/product/portal references: every repository match


Names include Adler One/Pro, their legacy anchor names, MyCoverVault, Os Meus Seguros, vault references, policy-management and AI-related wording. URL/anchor/asset names can outlive visible product branding. Support/neutral/distraction assessments are in §16; no external platform code or account was accessed. Raw references in site configuration are not proof of a live portal.

Investidores e family offices dos Estados Unidos olham para o país como uma porta de entrada estável na Europa: clima, segurança, qualidade de vida, um setor turístico em expansão e ativos imobiliários de luxo com valorização consistente. De Lisboa ao Algarve, da Comporta ao Douro, multiplicam-se vilas de prestígio, resorts, hotéis boutique e estruturas societárias criadas para enquadrar estes investimentos.

- [public/blog/investimento-americano-luxo-portugal/index.html:842](../public/blog/investimento-americano-luxo-portugal/index.html#L842): O que está a atrair o capital americano para o luxo português

- [public/blog/investimento-americano-luxo-portugal/index.html:845](../public/blog/investimento-americano-luxo-portugal/index.html#L845): Imobiliário de luxo em Lisboa, Cascais, Comporta e Algarve, com forte procura internacional

A boat laid up is not, and a surprising share of losses — fire, theft, storm damage, cradle failure, damage during lifting — happen in exactly that period. It also breaks continuity, and continuity is one of the things an underwriter looks at when pricing the renewal — along with the survey history, which is where a boat that sat unused and unmaintained for two winters tends to show up.

It is a practical observation: households with a home in one insurer's hands, a car with another, health cover arranged somewhere else, and a life policy from years ago — each bought at a different time, by a different route, sometimes in a different language — end up with gaps and overlaps that nobody notices until a claim, because nobody has ever looked at the whole picture at once.

- [public/en/private-clients-spain/index.html:416](../public/en/private-clients-spain/index.html#L416): What does "private client" mean here — is this a luxury product?

- [public/en/professional-liability-insurance-portugal/index.html:2155](../public/en/professional-liability-insurance-portugal/index.html#L2155): We're an insurance broker registered with the ASF, not tied to a single insurer. We work with a select panel of international insurers — chosen for the contract terms they offer and how they respond to a claim, not for the cheapest premium — and recommend what actually fits your activity. Free, and with no obligation.

- [public/en/professional-liability-insurance-portugal/index.html:2356](../public/en/professional-liability-insurance-portugal/index.html#L2356): A meaningful premium difference on the same risk almost always comes down to one of these: capital contracted, legal defence included within the capital rather than on top of it, an absent or insufficient retroactive date, and a narrower declared scope of activity than the actual practice. We review any competing quote free of charge and tell you exactly where the difference lies — even if the conclusion is that you should keep the other one.


</details>
